You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The unemployment rate is 9.8%, which points to late 2009 or 2010. Industrial production is +5.38% YoY, so the economy is in recovery. The 10-year yield is 3.38%, up 0.85 over 3 months, and the 2-year is 0.66%. Core CPI is 0.65% YoY, and the fed funds rate is 0.19%.

Candidate: December 2009. The 10-year was about 3.84% then, which is too high. In October 2009 it was about 3.38%, but the 3-month rise of 0.85 doesn't fit October, and unemployment in October 2009 was 10.0%.

Check the 10-year yield in 2010. It was 3.29% in December 2010, and unemployment was 9.8% in November 2010 and 9.4% in December. The 3-month rise of 0.85 fits a move from about 2.5% in September 2010 to about 3.4% in November. The November 2010 10-year average was around 2.76%, and the month-end was about 2.8%. December 2010 month-end was 3.29%, with unemployment at 9.4%, but the data as published in December 2010 would show the latest reading, November, at 9.8%. So the snapshot is December 2010.

Other checks: equities were up 24% over 6 months (July to December 2010), which fits. Gold was up 29% over 12 months, which fits. The VIX was 17.5, which fits December 2010. Core CPI was 0.65%, which fits (the low was around 0.6% in late 2010). Payrolls averaged 62k, which fits.
